sections.h2: What the Sheboygan County Register of Deeds handles
sections.html:
Every deed, mortgage and other land document for a parcel in Sheboygan County goes through this office. It also keeps vital records and files plats and Certified Survey Maps, and the land records it holds represent about $11 billion in real estate.

For a home seller, these are the services that matter:

  • Recording deeds, mortgages and liens, including federal tax liens.
  • Accepting new subdivision plats and Certified Survey Maps.
  • Registering births, marriages and deaths.
  • Handling the informal probate step called Termination of Decedent's Interest.
  • Collecting the state transfer fee and reporting it to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue.

Recorded land records are the basis of the real estate property tax, and the office reports transfer fee collections and property values to the Department of Revenue. County treasurer and real property staff, the planning office and the highway department all depend on it for information.

Recording most documents costs $30. State law fixes that price, so every Wisconsin county charges it. A house sale adds a state transfer fee of 30 cents on each $100 of value, or $3 per $1,000.

ServiceCharge
Recording most documents$30
Termination of Decedent's Interest$30 regardless of pages
Copy of a recorded document$2 for the first page, $1 for each added page
Certifying a copy$1 extra
Real estate transfer fee30 cents per $100 of value

The office posts a Fee Schedule page for its other charges, so check it before you send a check.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded in Sheboygan County?
sections.html:
You can record by mail or in person, or a title company or lender can record electronically. Under Wis. Stat. 706.05, an instrument offered for record must carry the signatures the law requires and identify the land and the parties well enough to be indexed. A document that affects a particular parcel must include the full legal description, and every conveyance of an interest in real property must come with the transfer return.

You file the return online with the Department of Revenue. Wis. Stat. 77.22 makes a completed return, plus the fee collection, a condition for accepting the deed. Nobody at the register must verify the value you report or the exemption you claim, which puts the accuracy on you.

Sheboygan County accepts e-recording through these vendors: CSC sRecording Solutions, ePN, Hopdox, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile. The system normally records, indexes and returns the image in about 24 hours. For paper documents, the office also offers SWIFT, a service that returns paper documents by email under an agreement with the county.

When a title company or lender handles your sale, ask which filing method they use, since that tells you when the recorded deed will come back.

sections.h2: Which Sheboygan County transfers pay no transfer fee?
sections.html:
Some transfers escape the state fee, and when one applies the deed must say so by citing the exemption. The full list is in Wis. Stat. 77.25. Homeowners run into these most:

  • Passing a property by will, descent or survivorship.
  • A foreclosure deed or deed in lieu of foreclosure handed to a mortgage holder or a land contract seller.
  • Family transfers between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild, made for little or nothing.
  • A transfer to or from a domestic partner.
  • A corrective or confirming deed for an earlier recorded conveyance, again for nominal or no consideration.
  • Any conveyance of real estate worth $1,000 or less.

An exemption does not cancel the paperwork. The transfer return is still filed. Both Termination of Decedent's Interest and Transfer by Affidavit (estates of $50,000 and under) call for an electronic return, and the affidavit gets recorded at this office only when real estate is involved.

sections.h2: Termination of Decedent's Interest, step by step
sections.html:
When a house passes after a death, this informal step can move title without a full probate case. It fits property held in joint tenancy, a life estate, survivorship marital property, a vendor's interest or a mortgagee's interest. You bring a copy of the document that shows that arrangement, the $30 recording fee and the electronic transfer return.

Sort out which route fits before you try to sell. If the register of deeds says the estate needs another path, such as Transfer by Affidavit, you will want to learn that before a buyer is waiting. A real estate attorney or the Register in Probate can answer what the register's office cannot.

Sheboygan County sits on Lake Michigan, and its cities are Sheboygan, Plymouth and Sheboygan Falls. The Census estimated 118,047 people in July 2025. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $232,700 (2020 to 2024), and owners occupy 71.5 percent of housing units. Rent has a median of $934, and household income a median of $73,094. If your parcel is on the lakefront or a river, ask the Register of Deeds for copies of any recorded easements or surveys before you list.

sections.h2: How can a Sheboygan County owner guard against deed fraud?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds offers a free Property Fraud Alert that monitors land records filed in the county; you sign up at propertyfraudalert.com. An email arrives when a document is recorded against your name or parcel, so you have time to respond.

The alert reports a filing after it is recorded, so it works as an early warning. Under Wis. Stat. 77.22(1) the register is not required to check the value or exemption on a transfer return, so the owner is the person best placed to notice a problem. If a filing looks false, call the Register of Deeds and ask what the document is, then talk to a real estate attorney and your title insurer.

sections.h2: What a seller should check before closing
sections.html:
Ahead of closing, pull the recorded deed that put you on title, check that its legal description matches the deed you will sign, and ask the title company who records and how. A house that came through a joint tenancy or a life estate may need a Termination of Decedent's Interest recorded first.

For questions about a specific document, contact the Register of Deeds directly. The office has forms for foreclosures and Sheriff deed guidelines on its Real Estate page.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Sheboygan County?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars covers most documents. The fee is set by statute and is the same statewide, and a Termination of Decedent's Interest also costs $30 however many pages it runs.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate transfer fee in Sheboygan County?
faqs.a: The seller does. Wis. Stat. 77.22(1) assigns the fee of 30 cents per $100 of value to the grantor, and the register takes it when the deed comes in.
Yes. The county works with CSC sRecording Solutions, ePN, Hopdox, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile, and e-recorded documents are normally recorded and returned in about 24 hours.

faqs.q: Do I need a transfer return when I inherit a house in Sheboygan County?
faqs.a: Yes. Inheritance by will, descent or survivorship is exempt from the fee under Wis. Stat. 77.25, yet the electronic return still goes to the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Can Sheboygan County alert me if someone records a document against my property?
faqs.a: Yes. Sign up for the register's free Property Fraud Alert at propertyfraudalert.com, and you are notified when something is recorded in your name or against your parcel.
